chunks: And from him, from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayna, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him):

He said: The obligatory and supererogatory prayers are fifty-one rak'ahs. Among them are two rak'ahs after the 'atama [night prayer] performed sitting, which count as one rak'ah while standing. The obligatory [prayers] among them are seventeen rak'ahs, and the supererogatory [prayers] are thirty-four rak'ahs.

key_terms.النَّافِلَةُ: supererogatory prayer (nafl/nawafil), voluntary prayers totaling 34 rak'ahs
key_terms.الْعَتَمَةِ: al-'atama, an archaic term for the 'Isha (night) prayer
key_terms.الْفَرِيضَةُ: obligatory prayer (fard), the five daily prayers comprising 17 rak'ahs
key_terms.رَكْعَةً: rak'ah, a single unit of Islamic prayer comprising standing, bowing, and prostration

ai.seo_question: How many rak'ahs are in the daily obligatory and supererogatory prayers according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that the combined daily obligatory (fard) and supererogatory (nafl) prayers total fifty-one rak'ahs — seventeen obligatory and thirty-four supererogatory. He specifies the ruling that the two rak'ahs performed sitting after the 'atama (night/'isha prayer) count as one rak'ah of standing prayer, clarifying how the fifty-one total is reckoned.
